title: Hardening the pipeline: runner permissions, isolation and trusted actions

videos.script: Every lesson so far gave the pipeline more power. It scans, it pushes, and since lesson 14 it signs. {{power}} That makes the pipeline worth attacking. A job holds a token, registry credentials and a signing key. Whoever can choose what the job runs gets all of them. {{surface}} This lesson writes linkbox's tests as a GitHub Actions workflow. First the way it is often written. {{careless}} A scanner called zizmor reads it and finds five problems. A dangerous trigger, a pull request title pasted into a shell, and actions named by tags that can move. Then you fix each one, and check every pin against the repository it names. {{fixed}} The scan becomes a stage, and a branch that brings a mistake back stops at it. {{stage}} Last, the machine underneath. Your own CI runs as a member of the docker group. On this laptop, that is the same as root, and the lesson says what that means for everything the pipeline holds. {{root}}
